Date: 2027-02-20T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Severe production regression — p99 spikes + 429 storms

Jordan —

We're seeing a production incident that started ~07:30 PT. Over the last 45 minutes our p95 for the inference route has moved from ~800ms to ~2.1s and p99 is spiking to 12–18s. At the same time we're seeing a correlated increase in 429 responses which seem to trigger aggressive retries from our side and client SDKs, amplifying the tail latency and causing request timeouts in our pipeline.

Impact: several customer-facing features are degraded (order matching / autocomplete). We're seeing 20% request failure rates and lots of timeouts. Attached is a small log bundle and a sample trace.

Can we get an urgent bridge and immediate mitigation? We can give you access to our org and logs if needed. We're on an hourly check for the weekend launch and this is high priority.

Attachments: server_logs_20270220.tar.gz (log bundle, 5MB)

Thanks,

On Sat, Feb 20, 2027 at 08:31 AM Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> Forwarding urgent report from Aurelia (see attached logs). Short summary: customer reporting p99 12–18s and a surge of 429s that appear to be feeding retries.

Triage update (initial):
- Observed pattern in our logs: sudden increase in concurrent short bursts; backend token consumption for the hosted API route hit a global hard-limit briefly at ~07:28 PT causing immediate 429s.
- Client-side behaviour: multiple clients (Aurelia SDK + their infra) issue immediate retries with fixed short backoff which produced a retry storm.
- Our rate-limiter change rolled 2027-02-19 22:10 PT increased per-tenant fairness but reduced per-connection token bucket depth (this likely reduced smoothing capacity).

Short-term mitigations I can apply now (5–10m):
1) Temporarily relax per-tenant burst limit for Aurelia by 2x to absorb backlog.
2) Apply a fast-fail + small jitter policy at our edge when queues exceed threshold (to reduce retry amplification).
3) Deploy a soft-queue path that converts some 429s into 202-queued responses for short-lived bursts.

I'm packaging a rate_limit_snapshot.json and will push a deployment patch if we have green on canary. Need Rishi to own the incident window and approve rollback if mitigation fails.

Attachments: rate_limit_snapshot.json

— Hannah

Subject: Incident update / proposed actions (incident lead)

On 2027-02-20 09:12 PT — incident lead summary:
- Metrics: global hosted-api p95 rose from 650ms -> 1.9s; p99 saw intermittent 12–18s spikes around 07:28–08:05 PT. Customer-specific token consumption shows sudden concentrated bursts.
- Hypothesis: combination of our recent rate-limiter rollout that shortened per-connection bucket depth + aggressive fixed-interval retries from several enterprise customers -> retry amplification.

Immediate action plan (executing now):
A) Apply emergency config: temporarily increase per-tenant burst depth for Aurelia + enable jittered exponential backoff enforcement via SDK gate (server-side header instructing SDKs to back off).
B) Add short-term throttle window: convert a subset of 429s to 202-queued for requests projected to finish within 2s (reduces retries).
C) Rollback consideration: if p99 does not improve within 30–45m, rollback the rate-limiter change from 2027-02-19 22:10 PT.

Operational notes:
- I've requested SRE to publish a grafana snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.net/d/abcd123/p99-spike
- Notifying Eng manager and CTO if we hit sustained SLA breach.

I'll coordinate the postmortem and timeline.

— Rishi Malhotra
Lead SRE / Incident Commander — Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-02-21T17:52:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary and next steps — Aurelia Health incident (2027-02-20)

Hi Lara / team —

Thank you for your patience and for sharing logs — wanted to summarize what we did and the next steps:

What happened (short):
- On 2027-02-20 morning, a combination of bursty client traffic and a recent rate-limiter change caused a brief period where our edge returned many 429s. Customer-side immediate retries amplified the tail latency (p99) and produced cascading timeouts for Aurelia.

What we did:
- Emergency mitigation: increased per-tenant burst depth for Aurelia and enabled jittered server-side backoff headers (reduced retry amplification).
- Mitigation outcome: p99 reduced from ~15s spikes to <1.8s within 20–30 minutes.
- Rollback path: we rolled back the specific rate-limiter parameter change on 2027-02-20 09:55 PT to restore smoothing capacity while we design a safer rollout.

Follow-ups / next steps:
- We will schedule a joint runbook session next week to tune client SDK retry recommendations (server-side instructs + SDK gating).
- Our postmortem will include telemetry changes: per-tenant burst health metric and alert for retry amplification patterns.
- As a gesture for the impact to your launch window, Marcus will follow up with a credit offer and an SLA review.

Attachments: grafana_p99_plots.png (snapshot), server_logs_20270220.tar.gz

If you'd like a 1:1 bridge to walk through the postmortem, I'm available tomorrow morning. Apologies again for the disruption — we take this very seriously.

Best,
Jordan Blake
